body:
Thinking Machines Lab is an artificial intelligence company co-founded by Mira Murati, formerly chief technology officer at OpenAI, together with other OpenAI alumni. It raised a US$2 billion seed round at a US$12 billion valuation within five months of starting, and its first product is Tinker, a tool for fine-tuning AI models.

The seed round

The round was led by Andreessen Horowitz, with investors including NVIDIA, Accel, ServiceNow, Cisco, AMD and Jane Street. It was among the largest seed rounds in Silicon Valley's history.

What Tinker is

Tinker is aimed at developers who want to fine-tune existing models without handling the cost and complexity of distributed computing. Reports put the company's annual revenue run rate at over US$100 million.

The valuation story

  • November 2025: Bloomberg reported talks at a valuation as high as US$55 billion to US$60 billion.
  • January 2026: reports said that round had not closed because backers wanted a stronger product record.
  • September 2026: TechCrunch reported that Accel was in talks to lead a US$1 billion round at a US$40 billion valuation.

Valuation talks are not completed rounds. Unless the company announces a close, treat those figures as reported negotiation.

Why it matters

The company is a test of whether a lab with a small product line can justify very large valuations, which is the question hanging over much of the AI funding market.
